verdict.rationale: Orama's pricing page calls Orama JS "The open-source search library," the docs refer to "Orama Open Source" as a distinct offering, and the library's code is in a public GitHub repository (github.com/oramasearch/orama). That makes the source readable. However, no evidence names the license or confirms its terms, and the openness applies only to the JS library, not to Orama Cloud or the on-prem context server. Missing for 10: an explicitly named OSI open-source license (e.g. a LICENSE file or license statement), confirmation of which components (Cloud, context server, runtime) are open versus proprietary, and independent corroboration of the license terms.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: The open-source search library. Add fast, relevant search to your own application at no cost.
so you can easily migrate your projects from **Orama Cloud** to **Orama Open Source** and vice-versa
